Directed on-the-ground execution and vendor operations for a fintech startup's SF headquarters, driving the physical transformation from shell to operational through real-time site adjustments, design compliance, and stakeholder walkthroughs
bullets.detail: A fintech startup's SF headquarters required a complete build-out across three floors with no general contractor overseeing the work, so vendor sequencing and dependency management were owned internally. I directed the on-the-ground execution, coordinating 15+ vendors and contractors, managing real-time site adjustments, and keeping the build aligned with design intent. When a structural blocker on Floor 3 made the planned electrical approach infeasible, I researched and proposed a surface-mounted alternative that preserved the timeline. Concurrent workstreams progressed without coordination-driven delays through the end of my contract in July 2026.

bullets.short: Designed and executed the full SF workplace experience — space planning, kitchen and amenity installation, AV infrastructure, signage, and furniture coordination — taking the office from shell to fully operational
bullets.detail: Beyond construction, I owned the experiential layer of the office: how the space looks, feels, and functions on day one. That spans space planning, kitchen and amenity installation, AV infrastructure, signage, and furniture coordination — translating design intent into installed reality. I made on-the-ground material and placement decisions in real time when the design firm wasn't present, keeping the build moving. The result was an office built from empty shell to fully operational without a dedicated project-management firm.

bullets.short: Drove cost optimization through contractor negotiations and creative problem-solving on build issues, consistently bringing proposals in under initial estimates and eliminating unnecessary change orders
bullets.detail: With 15+ vendors and no dedicated finance oversight, controlling spend was a core part of the role rather than an afterthought. I disputed a ~$9K electrical overquote by pushing for pricing transparency and identified ~$5K in savings by relocating electrical work on Floor 3. I also resolved a 44-fixture lighting delivery error with the vendor and electrician at no incremental cost while preserving UL certification, and caught a ~$1K overcharge by counting the actual meeting minutes in our Granola notes against the design firm's invoice and having it corrected. Across the project I consistently brought proposals in under initial estimates and eliminated unnecessary change orders.

New hires walked into a finished experience rather than a punch list.

Led end-to-end remodel of a modular event space — managed AV installation, secured electrical permits through the City of San Francisco, sourced and procured furniture via cross-country travel, and delivered the project $30K under budget; the space supports All-Hands, off-sites, and client events for 200+ employees
bullets.detail: Klaviyo's SF hub event space needed to flex between All-Hands, off-sites, and client-facing events for 200+ employees, which meant rethinking AV, layout, and furniture together. I led the remodel end-to-end — managing AV installation, securing electrical permits through the City of San Francisco, and traveling cross-country to source and procure the right furniture. By sourcing strategically and managing the vendor relationships directly, I delivered the full project $30K under budget. The finished space materially expanded how the office could be used without a larger build-out.

bullets.short: Designed the SF office environment including art curation and a full plant program, creating a biophilic, brand-aligned workplace that elevated the daily employee experience
bullets.detail: Beyond the event space, I shaped the broader feel of the SF office through art curation and a full plant program. The goal was a biophilic, brand-aligned environment that made the office somewhere people actively wanted to be, not just a place to work. These are the details that shape day-to-day employee experience even when they're not consciously noticed.

bullets.short: Stood up a brand-new SF office from scratch, sourcing and negotiating every vendor contract; managed an enterprise portfolio including CBRE, Knotel, and WeWork and partnered with building security and safety teams on access, inspections, and response protocols
bullets.detail: The SF office was mine to stand up from scratch: I sourced every vendor, negotiated every contract, and commissioned custom art in the company's brand colors. Operating inside an enterprise real-estate footprint meant managing relationships with major landlords and operators (CBRE, Knotel, WeWork) alongside Klaviyo's own contractors. I oversaw outside contractors and partnered with building security and safety teams on access control, inspections, and emergency response protocols: the less visible side of workplace operations that keeps the building's systems and the company's needs aligned.

bullets.short: Restructured facilities ticketing in Jira into a single intake that cut Office Support tickets ~20%, and documented the office's core processes in a written SOP others followed
bullets.detail: Office Support and Maintenance were auto-routing into each other in our Jira portal, so one request often created two tickets and volume looked nearly double what it was. I tracked the pattern, sat with our IT lead to map how the routing was configured, and made Office Support the single front door I triage and route, while re-pointing Maintenance straight to the building team. That cut Office Support tickets by about 20% and gave everyone one obvious place to submit anything. I also captured the office's core processes (onboarding, moves and setup, vendor and COI, and ticket intake) in a written SOP so the work didn't live only in my head.

bullets.short: Built an automated COI compliance tracker in Monday.com that auto-chases vendor renewals and files certificates itself, then scaled it to 8+ global offices, eliminating manual tracking
bullets.detail: Klaviyo's global real-estate team tracked vendor certificates of insurance by hand across many offices, so a lapse was always one missed date away. I diagnosed that the data existed but wasn't doing anything on its own, and built a self-running system in Monday.com: when a certificate nears expiration it auto-emails the vendor, the vendor's reply updates the record, and the new certificate files itself into the right category. I rolled it out from SF to 8+ offices worldwide, and it ran autonomously with no manual chasing.

bullets.short: Kept the office stocked on a weekly cadence down to the restroom amenities people still mention, and started an end-of-day happy hour ritual that still runs today
Served as central workplace point of contact and concierge for executive leadership (CFO, HR, Marketing) and 500+ employees across corporate and property management staff
bullets.detail: BRIDGE Housing's office ran through me as the central point of contact for both executive leadership and a 500+ person organization spanning corporate and property management staff. That meant balancing high-touch concierge support for the CFO, HR, and Marketing leads with the steady operational needs of the broader team. The role demanded constant prioritization and independent judgment — knowing what to handle immediately, what to schedule, and what to escalate.

bullets.short: Launched a break-room concessions program and in-office engagement initiatives that increased on-site attendance by 35% and strengthened company culture
bullets.detail: In-office attendance was lagging, so I treated it as an experience problem rather than a mandate problem. I launched a break-room concessions program and a set of in-office engagement initiatives designed around what actually brought people in. The combination increased on-site attendance by 35% and noticeably strengthened day-to-day culture.

bullets.short: Managed vendor relationships, supervised outside contractors for facility services, security, and safety, and partnered with IT via Jira to streamline service ticket submission and reduce operational redundancies
bullets.detail: Vendor accountability at BRIDGE meant reading the paper, not just managing the relationship. The clearest example: our snack-and-drink vendor charged a flat $2,000 a month, and when I read the invoices line by line I found they were buying from Costco and marking it up roughly 3x. I switched us to buying direct on the same budget, tripling the value and creating a kitchen culture the team still uses. Day to day, I supervised outside contractors for facility services, security, and safety, and partnered with IT in Jira to streamline ticket intake.

bullets.short: Supported board-of-directors meetings end-to-end: room setup with the executive assistant, lunch coordination, and full pre-meeting IT testing with live standby support
bullets.detail: Board meetings are zero-mistake events. I set the room with the EA, coordinated the lunches, and ran a full IT test beforehand with someone on standby during the meeting in case a board member needed help live. The goal was for leadership to never have to think about logistics: they walked into a room that simply worked.

bullets.short: Led BRIDGE's ~300-person HQ relocation from 550 to 350 California, delivered 17% under budget with zero downtime
bullets.detail: I was the hub keeping the move's workstreams sequenced, One Workplace on furniture, Crown on the physical move, and IT on the network, against a hard return-to-office date. I ran one master timeline in Excel plus a Monday.com board so everyone saw status, and I sequenced the dependencies so desks were built before move day: IT pre-set the Wi-Fi, then One Workplace delivered and installed the furniture, then the move was scheduled. On move day I was on-site at 550 California directing the movers and coordinating the new building's security and engineering, and I kept the loading dock open late so the crew finished in a single day. The team came back Monday to fully set-up desks and live Wi-Fi: zero downtime, and the move came in 17% under budget.

bullets.short: Owned the migration that moved BRIDGE off Iron Mountain to Corodata (a SOC 2/HIPAA-certified provider), cutting annual records-storage spend by more than half
bullets.detail: The CFO assigned me to a records-management overhaul: the CTO led digitization, the special projects manager and I co-sourced Corodata, and I owned the vendor migration. I audited our Iron Mountain contract and inventory, priced and negotiated the exit (about 10% off after a line-by-line invoice review), then ran the secure transfer of decades of sensitive records, resident files, building records, and blueprints, and verified the new facility met compliance for that data. It cut annual records-storage spend by more than half, and the savings were big enough that we then consolidated scattered records from every property into the new provider. I would rather over-respect that kind of sensitivity than under-respect it.

bullets.short: Implemented OptiSigns digital signage system, reducing annual spend by $15K while delivering expanded features; the company adopted the solution across all locations
bullets.detail: The existing signage approach was both costly and limited, so I evaluated alternatives and selected OptiSigns as a more flexible, lower-cost system. I managed the rollout from vendor selection through deployment, delivering expanded features alongside the savings. The switch reduced annual spend by $15K and worked well enough that the company adopted it across all locations.

bullets.short: Owned AV and IT infrastructure for all conference rooms and Zoom-enabled meeting spaces across two sites (SF and San Mateo), managing network, print, and digital signage services
bullets.detail: Across two sites in SF and San Mateo, I owned the AV and IT infrastructure that meeting spaces depend on — conference room AV, Zoom-enabled rooms, network, print, and digital signage. The priority was reliability: making sure the technology never became the reason a meeting didn't start on time. I'm not a dedicated IT specialist, but I'm comfortable owning these systems operationally and partnering with IT on deeper technical work.

bullets.short: Served as primary liaison with building management, security, and safety teams, coordinating maintenance, inspections, vendor services, and real-time incident response, including a solo elevator emergency during a paid event
bullets.detail: I was the liaison with building management, security, and safety, coordinating maintenance, inspections, vendor services, and real-time incidents. The sharpest example: during a paid member event, an Otis elevator broke down with no technician available. I went to the elevator room, got Otis on the phone, and when one car's alarm was blocking the second, I manually overrode and shut off the stuck car to free the working one, so the event kept running without interruption.

bullets.short: Became the unofficial asset manager: built a QR-code check-in/check-out system with a scanner, tying asset records to member CRM profiles for lease-end reconciliation and theft prevention
bullets.detail: Equipment was leaving with members at lease end and nobody could prove what went out versus what came back. I built my own fix: a QR-code check-in/check-out system with a scanner, with asset records tied to each member in our CRM. When a lease ended I could reconcile exactly what was outstanding. It started as a side project and made me the de facto asset manager for the space.

bullets.short: Drove member retention from open churn to 3.5% through proactive engagement programming, on-site events, and superior service delivery
bullets.detail: In a high-volume coworking environment, churn was a direct business metric, so I built proactive touchpoints to surface dissatisfaction before it became a cancellation. Through engagement programming, on-site events, and consistently strong service delivery, I brought retention from open churn down to 3.5%. The approach was retention-first: treat every member relationship as something to actively maintain.

bullets.short: Managed front-desk operations including reception, concierge services, visitor handling, shipping logistics, and member CRM (Nexudus) for a high-volume coworking environment
bullets.detail: Front desk at a high-volume coworking space is really a concierge business. Daily mail and package receiving ran through Envoy: scan the label, the member gets auto-notified, and the hand-off happens at the front. I onboarded new member groups and built the location guide (emergency exits, photos, the details people actually need on day one), and members used our team like their EAs for calendar management, meeting-room logistics, and lunch orders on the fly.
